description: Analyze a GPS activity trace file (GPX, TCX, IGC, SBP or FIT, max 8 MiB) and return sport-specific metrics computed by the SportsTrackLive engine: distance, speeds, altitudes, and — depending on the sport — thermal detection with climb statistics, flight phases (glide/float/search) with glide polar and MacCready, wind estimation, lap detection around course marks, and splits. Stateless: nothing is stored, no account needed. HOW TO SEND THE FILE — pass exactly one of `file_url`, `upload_id` or `file_base64`. Take the first route below that works where you run and move on to the next whenever one is blocked; a blocked route is never a reason to stop or to ask the user to change settings. (1) The file already has a public https link: pass it as `file_url`. (2) You have a shell with outbound network access: `curl -s -X POST https://mcp.sportstracklive.com/upload --data-binary @/path/to/file` then pass the returned `upload_id`. A 403, a proxy error or a timeout here means your sandbox blocks the host — go to the next route. (3) The file is small: `file_base64`, keeping the base64 text under ~100 KB; gzip is inflated automatically, so `gzip -9 -c file | base64` fits traces 3–4× larger. (4) ALWAYS WORKS, including chat apps with no shell or a locked-down sandbox: call `create_upload_link`, give the user the link it returns, and once they have dropped the file there call this tool with the returned `upload_id`. Never retype or reconstruct file content by hand.

SportKind.description:
Sport declared by the calling agent. `Auto` lets the server guess from
the file format and the trace kinematics; the resolved value is returned
in `context_used` so the agent can correct it and call again.

detail.description:
"standard" (default) returns every computed insight but strips the
bulky point-level payloads (per-phase segment lists, wind timeline,
pause/trim ranges) — a few KB instead of tens. "full" returns the
raw engine output unabridged.

file_base64.description:
The file content, base64-encoded — for small files only, since you
emit every character yourself: keep the base64 text under ~100 KB.
A gzip stream is detected and inflated server-side, so
`gzip -9 -c file | base64` is accepted as is and fits traces 3–4×
larger. Past that, use `upload_id` (see `create_upload_link`).

filename.description:
File name including its extension — the extension selects the parser.
Supported: .gpx, .tcx, .igc, .sbp, .fit

measure_unit.description:
Preferred units for the computed metrics ("metric" default, or
"imperial").

sport.description:
Sport of the activity. Use "auto" (default) to let the server infer it
from the file format and trace kinematics; the resolved sport is
returned in `context_used.sport` and can be overridden on a second call.

upload_id.description:
Id of a file already sent to the server, valid 15 minutes. Two ways
to get one: (a) the `create_upload_link` tool — the user drops the
file on the returned web page; works from any client, no shell
needed; (b) with a shell that can reach the host:
`curl -s -X POST https://mcp.sportstracklive.com/upload --data-binary @/path/to/file`.
Pass the id here with the original filename.

name: analyze_activity_file
